title: Live broadcasts over native WebRTC — browser test report
summary: LiveKit was replaced by native WebRTC (one-to-many P2P from the host's browser) with signalling relayed by the API over Reverb private channels. This run drives two browser contexts: the admin studio publishes Chromium's fake camera and microphone, a guest storefront viewer joins over WebRTC and plays real frames, then the host ends the show. Every step passed.
environment: API + Blade panels http://localhost:8000 / http://admin.nawy.test:8000 (php artisan serve)
Reverb ws://localhost:8080 (php artisan reverb:start); panels built with VITE_REVERB_ENABLED=true
ICE: STUN only (host candidates on the same machine); no TURN

flows.name: Host goes live from the admin studio; a guest watches over WebRTC; host ends the show
flows.goal: Prove the D18 design end to end: studio publish, join + peer token, signalling over Reverb, P2P media, end-of-show signal.
flows.preconditions: Seeded e2e admin; UAE market; Reverb running.

steps.action: Admin switches the panel to the UAE and creates a live broadcast
Start the camera in the studio (fake camera + mic)
Guest opens the storefront watch page
The host's video reaches the viewer over WebRTC
The studio lists the connected viewer and the upload estimate
The viewer is told the show ended

notes: Viewer and host run in separate browser contexts (no shared cookies); the viewer is a guest and authorises its private peer channel with the signed peer token.
The capacity cap (stream_full), token expiry, channel authorisation and TURN credentials are covered by Pest (tests/Feature/LiveWebRtcTest.php); the viewer state machine by Vitest.
